key_insight: LeapAlign enables reward-based fine-tuning of flow-matching generative models at any generation step by building two-step (leap) trajectories, allowing gradients to reach early steps without the memory blowup or gradient explosion of backpropagating through long trajectories.
problem_solved: Directly backpropagating reward gradients through long flow-matching generation trajectories is memory-intensive and unstable, preventing effective updates to early steps that determine global image structure.
method: Construct short two-step “leap” trajectories that bridge distant generation states so gradient signals can be propagated across long horizons with only local (two-step) backpropagation.
Perform post-training reward fine-tuning through these two-step transitions to stabilize gradients and dramatically reduce memory requirements compared to full-trajectory backpropagation.
Apply the leap mechanism at arbitrary generation steps so early- and mid-stage updates are possible without retraining or truncating the full generation process.
impact: Provides a practical, memory-efficient way to align flow-matching generative models with human preferences and to improve global structure in generated outputs—useful for practitioners who need targeted post-training edits without heavy compute or instability.

paper_title: LeapAlign: Post-Training Flow Matching Models at Any Generation Step by Building Two-Step Trajectories
paper_authors: Zhanhao Liang, Tao Yang, Jie Wu, Chengjian Feng, Liang Zheng
